learned: lstm_v1 seed 11: PR-AUC 0.0437 (best of the three seeds), ROC 0.668, best epoch 10; validation loss minimum at epoch 3 — PR-AUC peaks after the loss minimum, so early stopping on loss would have stopped too early; the metric, not the loss, is the right stopping signal for a 1 % prevalence problem.

lstm_v1 seed 22: PR-AUC 0.0226, best epoch 4. Same configuration, half the PR-AUC of seed 11 → seed variance (sd 0.012) is as large as most hyper-parameter effects; nothing below ±0.012 can be claimed as an improvement.
lstm_v1 seed 33: PR-AUC 0.0253. Three-seed mean 0.0305 ± 0.0115; ROC stable 0.64–0.67 while PR-AUC varies — the ranking of the bulk is stable, the ranking of the few top windows is not.

UNSUCCESSFUL: lr 1e-4 → PR-AUC 0.0213, ROC 0.545, best epoch 1 of 6: with 10× smaller steps the model barely moved from initialisation before patience expired; under-trained, not over-regularised (train loss still falling). Lower learning rate needs a longer patience/epoch budget we did not have on CPU.
UNSUCCESSFUL: lr 3e-4 → 0.0201, ROC 0.557, best epoch 1: same under-training pattern as 1e-4; confirms the default 1e-3 sits at the low end of the usable range for this budget.
lr 3e-3 → 0.0278, ROC 0.676: within seed noise of v1; higher ROC, lower PR-AUC — faster steps give a similar bulk ranking but a noisier top of the ranking.

lr 1e-2 → 0.0225, ROC 0.673: expected to diverge, did not — Adam's per-parameter normalisation plus LayerNorm kept training stable at 10× the default lr. Expectation recorded as wrong; PR-AUC at the bottom of the seed band.

batch 32 → 0.0266 (within noise), 2.2× slower per epoch (2902 s). Noisier gradients did not help; recall@1 % FAR 0.062 is the highest in the lr/batch studies, suggesting slightly different top-ranking but no net gain.
batch 512 → 0.0294 (within noise); 4446 s because fewer, larger steps need more epochs (best epoch 14). Batch size is not a lever here.

2 LSTM layers (137,513 params) → 0.0432, ROC 0.655: equal to v1 seed 11 (0.0437) at 1.9× the parameters and 1.8× the time. Depth does not add signal; the 60-minute sequence has little hierarchical structure to exploit.
hidden 32 (33,065 params) → 0.0301, ROC 0.661: within noise of v1 at half the parameters — capacity is not the bottleneck.
hidden 128 (195,881 params) → 0.0381, ROC 0.666, 6045 s: no gain for 2.8× parameters and 4× time; train loss lower, val loss higher (0.3308) → the extra capacity goes into fitting noise.

mean+max pooling over time → 0.0411, ROC 0.649: within noise of last-state pooling; order-insensitive pooling loses nothing, consistent with the finding that WHICH messages appear matters more than their order.
dropout 0.1 → 0.0255, ROC 0.678: less regularisation, higher ROC, lower PR-AUC; val loss minimum earlier (epoch 3) — mild over-fitting of the top of the ranking.
dropout 0.5 → 0.0379, ROC 0.642, recall@1 % 0.073 (highest in the study): heavier regularisation trades bulk ranking (ROC) for the head of the ranking. Within noise on the primary metric.

LayerNorm removed → 0.0288, ROC 0.677: within noise. The [embedding ‖ log count ‖ log Δt] scales are already comparable after log1p, so normalisation is not critical here; kept for stability at high lr (see lr 1e-2).

UNSUCCESSFUL: SGD+momentum lr 0.01 → 0.0218, ROC 0.645, best epoch 20 of 25 and still improving: without adaptive step sizes the rarely-updated embedding rows and the gate biases learn slowly; needs far more epochs than the CPU budget allows.

UNSUCCESSFUL on the operating point: SGD lr 0.1 → ROC 0.694 (best ROC of the whole study) but PR-AUC 0.0217 and recall@1 % FAR = 0: SGD learned the bulk ranking well but never pushed any positive into the top 1 % of scores — large uniform steps flatten the score distribution. Illustrates why PR-AUC, not ROC, is the primary metric.
AdamW wd 1e-2 → 0.0305, ROC 0.663: decoupled weight decay behaves like Adam here (within noise); the model is small and dropout already regularises.

pos_weight 1 (no class weighting) → 0.0277, ROC 0.683: within noise; the val loss (0.0655) is not comparable with weighted runs. Class weighting is not needed for ranking metrics with Adam, only for threshold behaviour.
pos_weight = full ratio (~65) → 0.0326, ROC 0.671: expected to over-fire (saturated scores) — it did not; scores shift up but the ranking is unchanged. Expectation recorded as wrong.

UNSUCCESSFUL: 6-hour local window → 0.0205, ROC 0.647, best epoch 2: longer history adds no precursor information (the failing unit is silent before most failures) while diluting the recent lines; early stop after 2 epochs = nothing learnable beyond v1.
UNSUCCESSFUL: 24-hour local window → 0.0210, best epoch 1: same as 6 h; confirms the signal is in the last hour and in the machine-wide channel, not in the unit's longer history.

UNSUCCESSFUL: 1-D CNN (kernels 3/5/7 × 64, masked max-pool) → 0.0234, ROC 0.601 — the worst architecture; it reached best epoch 20 of 25 and was still slowly improving. Local n-gram patterns over collapsed items carry less than the LSTM's whole-window state; max-pooling discards the repeat-count/Δt context.

Frozen MiniLM text embeddings → 0.0327, ROC 0.677: within noise of v1 on seed 11 but selected as the final model on MECHANISM before the test (it can represent messages never seen in training; 61 % of test lines are unseen). Later shown to reduce seed variance 0.0115 → 0.0004.

Ablation: failure-history only — at/below chance on validation (ROC 0.43–0.52) but ROC 0.68–0.74 on test: the validation period had unusually little failure recurrence (shift_analysis.md); the single most consequential finding for why the ANN (built without history) lost on test.
